standard_prerequisites.name: The universal property of truncation
standard_prerequisites.statement: A map from a type into a mere proposition extends to a map from its truncation, and the extension sends a projection to the value of the original map.
standard_prerequisites.use: It produces the map from the truncation of P back to P out of the identity map of P.

standard_prerequisites.name: Mere propositions and their path spaces
standard_prerequisites.statement: In a mere proposition any two elements are equal, and a map between mere propositions is an equivalence as soon as it has a section on one side.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is what makes the two maps quasi-inverses and hence the comparison an equivalence.

core_obligations: Give the map from P to its truncation, which is the projection and exists by definition (source line 813).
Apply the universal property of the truncation to the identity map of P, which is legitimate because P is a mere proposition, to obtain a map from the truncation of P back to P (source line 814).
Conclude that the two maps are quasi-inverses, which makes the comparison an equivalence, by the cited equivalence criterion for mere propositions (source line 815).

proof_roadmap.step: The projection gives P into the truncation.
The universal property gives the map back; the equivalence criterion closes the comparison.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source lines 809-811: a mere proposition is equivalent to its truncation. The proof (source lines 812-816) is short but it is a construction rather than a pointer: one direction is the projection, the other is the universal property of the truncation applied to the identity map, and that application is exactly where the hypothesis that P is a mere proposition is consumed; the two maps are then recognised as quasi-inverses by a cited criterion. Identifying the two maps and seeing which hypothesis licenses the extension is the substance, and the statement alone shows none of it.
